plan: [ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With value $30, bidding 30 ensures we win exactly when the highest competing bid is below 30, paying that second-highest price, yielding nonnegative profit. There’s no prior-round info to adjust strategy. Bids are in $0.1 increments, so 30.0 is valid. ]

[ In a second-price auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit by ensuring you win exactly when the second-highest bid is below your value and pay that second-highest bid. With no prior rounds to learn from and values redrawn independently, there’s no benefit to shading or inflating. I will bid exactly my value: 35.0. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy because your bid only affects whether you win, not the price you pay. With value $6 (uniform 0–49), optimal is to set your maximum acceptable price to 6. If others bid below 6, I win and pay the second-highest bid; if above, I lose and pay 0. No prior rounds to learn from. Tie at 6 resolves randomly; still optimal to bid 6. ]
